title: Cloud Connector placement across regions: centralized, decentralized, overlapping address space

prose.label: Failure across regions.
prose.text: Failover between Service Edges is described per Cloud Connector, not across cloud regions: [[cloud-connector.overview.gateway-failover]]. Whether workloads in one region can fail over to Cloud Connectors in another, other than by routing changes, is not stated {{gap:cross-region-failover}}.

prose.label: Overlapping address space.
prose.text: How namespaces keep tag mappings apart when AWS address ranges overlap: [[cloud-connector.workload-discovery.namespaces]]. {{azure-peering-duplicate-stack}}
Cost and latency trade-offs of each layout are cloud-provider matters the captured sources do not state {{gap:placement-guidance}}.

checks.do: Whether the workload's region has its own Cloud Connector group or reaches one in a hub region through a transit gateway or virtual WAN hub.
In Azure with VNet peering and overlapping CIDRs, whether a separate Cloud Connector group stack serves each overlapping set.

egress-groups.statement: In most cases Cloud Connector is deployed into groups or locations that serve the same internet egress.

quotes: In most cases, Cloud Connector is deployed into groups or locations that serve the same internet egress.

region-independence.statement: Deployments may be centralized, using AWS Transit Gateway or Azure Virtual WAN Hub, or decentralized, with each VPC or VNet having direct internet access; either way each region serves its own egress points for Cloud Connector and is not affected by other regions, even during a cloud provider outage.

quotes: Whether centralized, using AWS Transit Gateway or Azure Virtual WAN Hub, or decentralized, where each Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) or Azure Virtual Network (VNet) has direct internet access,
each region serves a number of different egress points for Cloud Connector and does not affect other regions even if there is a cloud provider outage.

azure-peering-duplicate-stack.statement: In Azure the same CIDR block can be reused in a deployment, but with VPC peering endpoints cannot separate the traffic, so the Cloud Connector group stack must be duplicated.

quotes: When deploying applications in Azure, you can reuse the same CIDR block in a deployment. When using VPC peering, you cannot use endpoints to separate traffic. You must duplicate the Cloud Connector group stack.

cross-region-failover.title: Failover of workloads to Cloud Connectors in another region
cross-region-failover.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "There is no automatic cross-region CC failover — a workload VPC in us-east-1 does not automatically reroute through us-west-2 CCs if the us-east-1 group fails. Cross-region recovery requires either a hub-spoke TGW topology or operator-managed route-table changes"; and a Cloud Connector failing over its Service Edge tunnel "does not route through US PSEs unless the subcloud config permits it".

placement-guidance.title: Same-region placement and the cost of centralized egress
placement-guidance.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Cloud Connector should always be deployed in the same region as the workloads it serves"; cross-region traffic incurs data-transfer charges and latency; Transit Gateway attachment and inter-region charges apply to hub designs; decentralized designs need more instances and "more egress IPs to register with ZIA". These rest on cloud-provider pricing and design advice, not on a captured Zscaler source.
